subject: Demo follow-up: contrast tests & hallucination triage
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Stone <ariel@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Demo follow-up: contrast tests & hallucination triage

Hi Ariel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the demo: we heard three primary asks from you and the team:

- A direct quality comparison vs the hyperscaler endpoint you referenced (CloudWave) focused on hallucination frequency and factuality on domain prompts.
- A short, repeatable probe you can run in your sandbox plus a Redwood-run sweep to validate results.
- Estimated latency/cost delta for the same prompt set at 1000 concurrent requests (rough order-of-magnitude).

Proposed plan (48–72 hour initial sprint):
1) Run a 1000-prompt probe (subset attached: hallucination-probe-prompts.csv) using our eval harness and CloudWave’s public endpoint to capture hallucination rates, top-k differences and token-level delta.
2) Surface regression checks on your two highest-priority intents (support triage + doc-extraction) with exact-match and F1 where applicable.
3) Produce a 1–2 page exec summary + a short recording of the Redwood test run (demo-recording.mp4).

Questions for you:
- Would you prefer Redwood to run the probe end-to-end and share results, or would you like the prompts and harness to run it internally first?
- Any additional constraints on data (PII removal, IP ranges) we should be aware of for the sandbox?

If that works I’ll kick off the internal tasks and loop procurement for the pricing/cmps side. I’ve attached the prompt set and the demo recording stub.

Thanks —

Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (video, 12MB stub), hallucination-probe-prompts.csv (CSV, 120 rows)
From: Ariel Stone <ariel@nebulacorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulacorp.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: contrast tests & hallucination triage

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers/questions from our side: 

- We’d appreciate if Redwood ran the initial sweep and shared the raw logs + summary. That helps us triage faster.
- Sandbox constraints: no customer PII in prompts (we can scrub), and ideally connections from the 10.11.0.0/16 range only.
- On pricing: our procurement team will need a rough delta vs CloudWave (per-token / per-hour estimate) just to scope internal approvals — a ballpark is fine for now.

Can you confirm you can deliver the initial sweep and summary by end of day Tuesday (48 hrs)? If so we’ll schedule a short 30-min sync with procurement on Wednesday to discuss the procurement path and any NDA redlines.

—Ariel
VP Product, NebulaCorp

>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: contrast tests & hallucination triage

Dylan / Ben —

I’ll take point on running the Redwood sweep and producing the summary. Proposed breakdown: 

Phase A (quick probe, 24–48h):
- Run the 120-row prompt set on Redwood with our standard eval harness (measure hallucination flag, top-1 factuality, confidence cal).
- Hit CloudWave’s public endpoint for the same set (Ben to provision the CloudWave API key we used in the last benchmark).
- Output: raw CSV (prompt, redwood_out, cloudwave_out, hallucination_label, score_diffs) + short readout doc.

Phase B (regression & scoped load sim, 48–72h):
- Target the two intents Ariel flagged. Generate 300 synthetic variations each (Ben), run exact-match / F1.
- Run a small load sim (200 QPS for 5 minutes) to capture latency P50/P95 under standing config; we should also try the smart-batching config to show unit-cost improvement.

Assignments:
- Marissa: run Redwood sweep, collate results, write exec summary, upload to Drive.
- Ben: spin-up CloudWave runs, share API key and results.
- Dylan: own the external comms and timeline; grab procurement contact and confirm IP range constraints.

Ben — can you confirm you have the CloudWave key and you can deliver CloudWave CSV by tomorrow EOD? I’ll start the Redwood runs now and post interim results to the Drive link (probe-matrix.xlsx).

Marissa
Sr PM, Developer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments: probe-matrix.xlsx (workbook stub)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Stone <ariel@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@nebulacorp.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: contrast tests & hallucination triage

Ariel —

Confirming plan and timeline: Redwood will run the Phase A sweep and deliver raw CSVs + a 1-page exec summary by EOD Tue (48 hours). We’ll respect your sandbox constraints (no PII, allowlist IPs — please share the exact IPs when convenient).

What you’ll get:
- Raw results (redwood_vs_cloudwave.csv) with hallucination labels + scoring deltas
- Short exec summary (1 page) highlighting top failure modes and a recommended next test matrix
- Recording of the Redwood run + instructions to re-run the probe locally in your sandbox
- Ballpark cost/delta: preliminary estimate attached to the summary (we’ll include per-token / hourly service delta; final pricing will follow procurement conversation)

HubSpot: we’ve updated the deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-NEB-0034). Proposed 30-min procurement sync Wednesday 2027-05-26 16:00 ET — does that time work for your team?

Links/Artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-probe-docs (interim results will land here).

Thanks —

Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
